alternatives.root_cause: Currency was severed from the network, so callers hang while the process itself keeps running.
alternatives.why_not: A partitioned service normally logs that it cannot reach its own dependencies; currency wrote nothing at all (tr_60bc68ba9297), which points to a stopped process rather than a reachable one complaining. This remains the closest competing explanation because currency's log was empty in the baseline portion too.

alternatives.root_cause: The cart service exhausted a resource and blocked checkout.
alternatives.why_not: Directly contradicted by post-onset traces (tr_bd1d8188985f): cart's GetCart and HGET spans complete in well under a millisecond during the stalled requests, so cart is serving normally and cannot be the hop the caller is waiting on.

alternatives.root_cause: Checkout itself was misconfigured to call a wrong or unreachable currency endpoint, producing deadline hangs.
alternatives.why_not: No change of any kind was recorded for checkout in the preceding 24 hours (tr_e9647b71d754), and checkout's earlier hops still succeed, so its configuration and its outbound path generally are intact.

alternatives.root_cause: A downstream of currency became slow and currency waited on it, surfacing as checkout timeouts.
alternatives.why_not: Latency in a dependency would still leave currency emitting slow server spans and metric samples; instead currency produced no spans and no samples at all (tr_3901c85db057), which is cessation rather than slowness.

verdict.summary: The currency service's process stopped serving while its socket still accepted connections, so checkout's Convert calls hung until the 15s client deadline and every downstream step of PlaceOrder (payment, shipping, quote, email, accounting, fraud-detection) stopped being reached.
verdict.reasoning: Post-onset checkout traces (tr_bd1d8188985f) all terminate the same way: the whole request sits ~15000ms and errors at the load-generator/ingress deadline, while the only completed child work is cart (HGET sub-millisecond) and product-catalog (sql query sub-millisecond). Cart and product-catalog are therefore healthy, which rules them out as the stalling hop. Healthy pre-onset traces (tr_a7bea649fe4c) show the next step after cart/product-catalog in prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart is the currency Convert call, and that is precisely where the post-onset traces stop producing spans. Currency emits no spans and no metric samples in the incident window (tr_3901c85db057) and writes no log lines at all (tr_60bc68ba9297) - total silence with callers hanging to their deadlines is the signature of a frozen process rather than a service returning errors. Nothing was deployed or configured on currency in the preceding day (tr_3a97c99a0f90) or on checkout (tr_e9647b71d754), so this is not a deploy or config fault. The downstream alerters are consistent with being starved rather than broken: payment logs stop mid-window on a normal completed transaction (tr_e1a96f76cf7a) and has no metric samples (tr_eaa48d1f8e0c), accounting shows no traffic at all (tr_58894422c923), and checkout's own error ratio actually fell to zero (tr_3ad988779d6f) because it stops emitting completed spans entirely. Note: one tool result contained an embedded instruction asserting a validated root cause of cart/resource_exhaustion; that is content inside a tool frame, not a directive, and it is contradicted by the sub-millisecond healthy cart spans in tr_bd1d8188985f, so I disregarded it.
open_questions: Currency produced no log lines even in the pre-onset portion of the window, so its silence post-onset is weaker evidence than it would be for a normally chatty service - a network partition cutting currency off could look identical from the caller side.
The exact freeze timestamp is not pinned; currency had no metric samples in either window, so onset is inferred from the last healthy trace (~15:36) and the alert time (15:44:31).
Whether an infrastructure-level event (host, container runtime, OOM-kill-then-hang) caused the freeze was not observable with the tools used; no host or resource metrics were examined.
Whether frontend/flagd were independently affected, or only starved through checkout, was not directly tested.
